finding.claim: authorize() is async but is not awaited in DELETE /reports/:id, so the permission check never blocks the delete. Any authenticated user can delete any report.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id (req.params.id).

trace.note: report is fetched by the attacker-supplied id with no owner scope
authorize(...) returns a Promise that is neither awaited nor caught
authorize is async, so the 403 throw becomes a rejected promise instead of a synchronous exception
db.reports.remove runs immediately without waiting for the check, so the delete happens regardless of grants

finding.guards_checked: The only guard on the path is authorize() at line 20, and its result is ignored. The rejection is also unhandled, which can crash the process on Node 15+ or leave an unhandled-rejection warning. The PUT handler at line 27 does await authorize, which shows the intent. No other middleware performs authorization; the global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:20 (async, throws 403 at :11-14) but its Promise is not awaited, so the check never blocks; the global middleware at :4-7 only copies the session user.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() (defined at :9-16) without await, so db.reports.remove at :21 runs regardless of the grant check, and any session user can delete any report, while the PUT handler at :27 does await it.

finding.claim: Mass assignment: the whole client JSON body is passed to db.reports.update in PUT /reports/:id. A user with write permission on a report can overwrite any field, including owner, id or tenant fields.
finding.source: The req.body JSON of PUT /reports/:id, fully attacker-controlled.

trace.note: express.json() parses the body into an arbitrary object
authorize checks only the 'write' grant, not which fields may be written
req.body is passed to update with no field allowlist

finding.guards_checked: There is no allowlist, schema validation or field filtering. The authorize check covers only whether the user may write the report, not which fields. The impact depends on the db.reports.update implementation, which is not in this code, so this is a candidate.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 (awaited at line 27, throws 403) checks only the 'write' grant. There is no field allowlist or schema validation.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: express.json() at server.js:3, the awaited authorize at :27 and the unfiltered req.body passed at :28. But db is never defined in this repo, so I can't tell whether db.reports.update (:28) ignores or filters fields such as owner, id or tenant, and the impact depends on that.
